_comment: Franchise ID -> GM name. Hand-maintained, and the one thing in this
pipeline that cannot be fetched: MFL's league response carries team names
but no owner_name for any franchise in 19716, so there is no machine link
from a franchise to the GM names the site displays.
IDs are stable across seasons; team names are not. 0001 has been 'FOX
Injury Time-Out Music' (2023), 'The GOAT' (2024), 'Uncle Rico' (2025) and
'Smells Like GOAT' (2026) — all Shak. Key on id, never on name.
This mapping was derived, not guessed. Each row was confirmed by replaying
past seasons through src/derive.mjs and matching the result against the
records already on the site: 0003's 2025 all-play record comes out to
116-24 .829 (Samson's recorded best), and the 2023 fold reproduces the
Fantasy Bowl at 142.36-125.67 exactly, fixing seeds 1-6 that year against
the recorded field order Samson, Andres, Asher, Shak, Vip, Raj. 2024 and
2025 agree independently.
0002 was Raj's franchise through 2024 and is Ryaan's from 2025 — confirmed
by the league: Ryaan replaced Raj, who is no longer in the league. The slot
changed hands; it was not a rename. If a GM leaves, update the row rather
than adding one — records follow the gm name, not the id. Raj's history
stays under 'Raj' in data.js and is untouched by this.
'gm' must match a name in the GMS list in weekly-log.js. Ingest fails loudly
on any unmapped id or unknown GM name rather than writing a wrong record.
_history_comment: Franchise ids are stable, but a slot can change hands. `history` pins the GM
for seasons where the current mapping above is wrong, so the lineup archive
can attribute a 2019 week to the man who actually played it.
Only 0002 has changed hands in the MFL era: Raj held it through 2024, Ryaan
from 2025. 0011 is Laura's, created by the 2025 expansion -- `since` keeps it
out of earlier seasons, where MFL confirms only 0001-0010 ever posted a score.
Verified the same way the mapping above was: replay each MFL season through
src/derive.mjs and check the derived top-six seed order against the playoff
field recorded in data.js. 2016-2019 and 2021-2025 reproduce their recorded
field exactly. 2020 reproduces the same six teams with seeds 4 and 5 swapped:
Vip and Imran both finished 64-53 and the recorded order puts Imran ahead
despite Vip holding 3.48 more points. The league confirms this is moot --
both had the record and the points to make the playoffs, and the bracket bore
it out, with Imran going on to win the whole thing and Vip reaching the
Fantasy Four. Nothing downstream reads 2020 seed order, and the lineup
archive never reads seeds at all.
2015 ran in a DIFFERENT MFL league (53720). The same ids mean the same GMs
there, verified by replaying it: the derived top six reproduces the recorded
field Dante > Hoss > Samson > Asher > Imran > Raj exactly, including the
three-way 53-64 tie that points for breaks in Raj's favour for the last spot.
